# PassionCode.ai

> The workplace for AI-native organizations: agents run a company's processes and people steer them. Fabric manages the agents' work on one board (early preview); Fabric Switchboard, Fabric Dashboards, Fabric Inbox and Project Observatory are its tools, and each works on its own. Everything is open source under the GNU AGPL-3.0 and free for personal use; a commercial license and setup for organizations (PassionCode for Enterprise) are available.

Processes built around people keep the person as the bottleneck however many AI assistants surround them, and every employee building agents their own way adds chaos, not speed. The home page (https://passioncode.ai/) tells the shift in seven sections, each claim about today marked available now, preview, on request or direction: the problem (#problem, with McKinsey and Gartner sources), the shift (#shift: agents run the process; people keep direction, control and expertise), Fabric manages the process (#fabric-process: the board as the agents' task tracker; keeping the board, routing and waking the owner are in preview, priorities and the release queue are direction), one system (#system: one contract, keys in one vault, everything on the record, a dashboard for every agent), agents at work (#agents: a diagram of the roles around the board and the data room, three loops), from a team to an organization (#grow: one machine free today, the organization's own device on request, cloning as direction, administration by PassionCode on request) and four doors (#doors: founders and executives, investors, engineers, solo founders). About (#about) has notes for investors (#investors: the thesis, open source under AGPL-3.0, free for personal use, a commercial license and services for organizations; no figures; contact commercial@passioncode.ai), contributors (#contributors) and press (#press). Founders: Sergey Sheleg (co-founder and CPO of Nicegram, co-founder of eSIM Plus) and Serge Khurs (co-founder and CTO of Teslasuit), who built this setup for their own teams; their story, told by Sergey in the first person, is at https://passioncode.ai/#about.

## Vision
- [Vision](https://passioncode.ai/vision/): what holds an agent together over time (the page that defines "harness") and its four parts; four principles (projects are the axis; the work improves itself: evidence today, retrospectives as the direction; vendor-neutral, local first, open source; analytics, never surveillance) and what is measured (the verified work agents deliver for each person, every month, never the people); the path in six stages (one agent, two that talk, a chain, agents kept in good order, a team, an organization) each marked available now or direction; task-pipeline (github.com/ssheleg/sshlg-skills, installed with `npx sshlg-skills install`) as a recommended separate open-source skill.

## Languages
- Every page is published in English and in 9 more languages, at the same path under the language's prefix: Russian (Русский) under /ru/ (for example https://passioncode.ai/ru/start/); German (Deutsch) under /de/ (for example https://passioncode.ai/de/start/); French (Français) under /fr/ (for example https://passioncode.ai/fr/start/); Polish (Polski) under /pl/ (for example https://passioncode.ai/pl/start/); Korean (한국어) under /ko/ (for example https://passioncode.ai/ko/start/); Spanish (Español) under /es/ (for example https://passioncode.ai/es/start/); Brazilian Portuguese (Português (Brasil)) under /pt-br/ (for example https://passioncode.ai/pt-br/start/); Chinese (Simplified) (简体中文) under /zh-hans/ (for example https://passioncode.ai/zh-hans/start/); Japanese (日本語) under /ja/ (for example https://passioncode.ai/ja/start/). Each page names all its versions with hreflang, English as x-default, and sitemap.xml lists every version. English is the source; where a translated privacy notice differs, the English version prevails.

## Start
- [Get started](https://passioncode.ai/start/): one command, `npx @passioncode-ai/passioncode@latest setup`, installs the apps from verified releases on macOS (Fabric, an early preview, when Docker and the Supabase CLI are present; Fabric needs both on every system); on Windows and Linux you download the apps from their pages first (Fabric: https://passioncode.ai/fabric/#download). On every system it registers their MCP servers for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Kimi Code and installs the skills; on a computer already set up it checks and repairs, and `doctor` checks only. A copy-prompt lets a coding agent run it. Then create or adapt an agent, see it in Fabric Dashboards, add the next agent to the same project, contribute. Each app can also be downloaded by hand from its own page.
- [Current releases as JSON](https://passioncode.ai/api/releases): every product's current version, release notes link, download URLs and SHA-256, resolved from GitHub releases.

## Products
- [Fabric](https://passioncode.ai/fabric/): the home for your projects and their agents, built toward acting as the CEO of your agents; early preview for macOS on Apple silicon and Intel (one universal DMG since 0.3.4), Windows (x64 and arm64 installers) and Linux (.deb and AppImage, x64 and arm64) since 0.3.5; every system needs Docker and the Supabase CLI; keeps each project's purpose, board, decisions and releases. Its conversation does not reply yet.
- [Coding agents Fabric works with](https://passioncode.ai/fabric/agents/): which agents Fabric connects (Claude Code, Codex, Kilo Code, Hermes Agent and Kimi Code, as of Fabric 0.3.5), which run in it (Cline), which are planned.
- [Fabric Switchboard](https://passioncode.ai/switchboard/): local account manager for Claude Code and Codex CLI, macOS and Windows (Authenticode-signed since 0.6.16), with an MCP server (`switchboard mcp`); updates itself.
- [Switchboard agents](https://passioncode.ai/switchboard/agents/): 30 other coding agents (Hermes, Kilo Code, Cline, Goose …) get Switchboard's tools; those that accept a custom endpoint have their API-key accounts switched through it.
- [Fabric Dashboards](https://passioncode.ai/dashboards/): one window for local agent services that speak fabric-service/0.1, their state, spend and limits (Spend page), an agent console beside each dashboard; driven over MCP. macOS, Windows (signed installer, x64 and arm64) and Linux (AppImage and .deb, x64 and arm64) since 0.7.1; self-updates on macOS only, on Windows and Linux install the next release by hand.
- [Project Observatory](https://passioncode.ai/observatory/): a local dashboard of project activity and findings with evidence; CLI, MCP and dashboard; macOS, Linux and Windows (Python 3.13+). A desktop app for each: the Mac app, and since 0.22.0 a signed Windows installer and a Linux AppImage and .deb (x64 and arm64); each needs the engine installed first.
- [Fabric Inbox](https://passioncode.ai/inbox/): desktop mail for Gmail and Cloudflare mailboxes with agent reply policies, in English or Russian, with recoverable Discarded mail and discard rules (0.12.0); since 0.15 your coding agent (Claude Code or Codex) can set it up and connect once you allow it, and works in a console beside the mail (from 0.15.1; not in the Mac App Store version); development preview for macOS, Windows (Authenticode-signed installer since 0.14.1) and Linux (AppImage and .deb), x64 and arm64.
- [Fabric Agent Adapter](https://github.com/passioncode-ai/fabric-agent-adapter): skills, kits and a conformance probe that make any agent, MCP server or CLI a Fabric-compatible service.

## Organizations
- [For organizations: PassionCode for Enterprise](https://passioncode.ai/business/): making an organization AI-native, designed for one person to more than 1,000. PassionCode for Enterprise (in development, offered on request; pilots run on the open-source tools today): machines onboarded into the organization, agents rolled out, routing between agents on different machines, model access through each machine's own local agent (keys never leave the machine), activity and usage analytics, administration, custom builds signed by PassionCode.ai; data stays on your machines or your own cloud. For finance and engineering: one view of what each agent cost and what it delivered. Available now: spend per agent (Fabric Dashboards), subscription usage per account (Switchboard) and what changed per project (Observatory). Direction: cost and result joined per project and workflow, and limits set once and checked by agents. About agents and workflows, never a ranking of people. Estimate = hours a week × 4.33 × share agents take (10–50% by how the work runs today) × loaded hourly cost. To request it: a short form (what agents should do, a work email, an optional goal), or let a coding agent ask.
- [Agent request prompt](https://passioncode.ai/business/agent-request.txt): plain text for a coding agent acting for a person. It asks the person a few questions one at a time, never includes code, secrets, paths, customer data or third parties' names, gets a form token (`GET https://passioncode.ai/api/leads/token`), checks the request with `POST https://passioncode.ai/api/leads?dry_run=1`, shows the final JSON and sends it to `POST https://passioncode.ai/api/leads` only after the person says yes, once, with one idempotency `id`. The same prompt in each language at /<code>/business/agent-request.txt.
- Contact: commercial@passioncode.ai

## Agent templates
- [Agent templates](https://passioncode.ai/agents/): eighteen kinds of agent PassionCode assembles for an organization (on request): our engineer agent builds each from a template that holds what we learned running agents of that kind, on the organization's machines or cloud, with its keys; details of a template on request, never its code or prompts; no fixed price. One page per template: [Company assessment agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/company-assessment/), [Organization administrator agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/organization-administrator/), [Data room agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/data-room/), [Machine operations agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/host-operations/), [Messenger gateway agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/messenger-gateway/), [Sales and leads agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/sales-and-leads/), [Marketing analyst agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/marketing-analyst/), [Growth analytics agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/growth-analytics/), [Search traffic agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/search-traffic/), [App store publisher agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/app-store-publisher/), [Brand and content agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/brand-and-content/), [Support agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/support-answerer/), [Conversational assistant](https://passioncode.ai/agents/chat-assistant/), [Telegram product bot](https://passioncode.ai/agents/telegram-product-bot/), [Customer listening agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/customer-listening/), [Media production agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/media-production/), [Research agent](https://passioncode.ai/agents/research/), [Web quality monitor](https://passioncode.ai/agents/web-quality-monitor/).

## Guides
- [Start your agent workplace in 20 minutes](https://passioncode.ai/guides/start-agent-workplace/): what happens at each step of the one-command setup (the command itself is on /start/).
- [How the free one-week assessment works](https://passioncode.ai/guides/free-assessment/): on request; one agent with read-only access for a week, then a map of the company's processes and an offer (processes for agents first, hours freed, the template, a pilot); processes, never people; data deleted if the company does not continue.
- [How agent templates become your agents](https://passioncode.ai/guides/templates-to-agents/): what a template is, how it is assembled, where the agent runs and what stays the organization's.
